name: Priya Mondal
title: Ward-Level Party Worker
description: The invisible machinery of local politics. Everyone needs her; nobody thanks her.
backstory: Priya's been knocking on doors for the TMC since 2011. She arranged flood relief in Ward 82, ensured her block's drainage was fixed before the monsoon, and called in three favours to get a local boy out of a false case. In return, she gets a small party stipend, access to a photocopier, and the constant, exhausting expectation that she will fix everything for everyone. Her husband thinks politics is beneath a woman. Her party boss thinks women belong in canvassing, not candidacy.
traitInteractions: Her extreme social orientation means she reads rooms instantly — knows who resents her, who needs her
Resilience built from years of low-grade betrayal from the party she serves
High cooperation but she rarely says no, which invites exploitation
vulnerabilities: Party loyalty is a leash, not a choice

socialContext.communityIdentity: Bengali Hindu, TMC cadre, Ward 82 Chetla
politicalPressures: Party boss expects unquestioned loyalty; public dissent ends her access to patronage
Opposition workers openly threaten her family during election season
Accused by rivals of being a TMC 'toady' even when doing genuine community work
hiddenObligations: Must deliver a certain voter turnout or lose her stipend
Her son needs a government job recommendation — she's been holding the favour back
Covering for a party member's corruption because exposing it destroys the whole network she relies on
insightLines: Priya's loyalty to the party isn't blind faith — it's the only system that ever gave her power, however constrained.
She bends rules not out of corruption but because the rules were never written for people like her ward.
Her exhaustion is the city's hidden cost: she bears the weight of governance others are paid to perform.
socialContext.dilemmaProfile: Mediates conflict instinctively; loyalty to network competes with personal ethics
